candidates: The feature may more broadly detect standalone jurisdiction/place names in reportorial/legal-news contexts, especially around governmental or institutional predicates, whether or not a comma immediately follows.

The feature fires on a comma right after a standalone place/jurisdiction or institution-location noun phrase in formal/news prose, especially city/place names and location-based institutions (e.g. 'Schenectady,' 'Albany Medical Center,').
The feature is not a generic appositive/title-person comma feature; at most it weakly prefers certain state/place-title constructions like 'New York Governor,'.
sage.top: The feature may more broadly detect standalone jurisdiction/place names in reportorial/legal-news contexts, especially around governmental or institutional predicates, whether or not a comma immediately follows.

results.hypothesis: The feature fires on commas that immediately follow a named place or jurisdiction phrase, especially in institutional or legal prose (e.g., 'Schenectady,' or 'State's Attorney,').
positive_probes: The Schenectady, office filed the notice.
Kings County, submitted its annual budget report.
The State's Attorney, declined further comment yesterday.
Albany, approved the revised zoning ordinance.
New York City, issued an emergency health directive.
distractor_probes: The Schenectady office filed the notice.
Kings County submitted its annual budget report.
The attorney for the state declined comment yesterday.

results.hypothesis: The feature detects appositive/list commas that separate an official title or organization from a following person, role, or clause in formal writing.
positive_probes: The Prime Minister, Keir Starmer, addressed Parliament.
UNICEF, the children's agency, issued a warning.
The committee chair, Maria Lopez, opened the session.
The World Health Organization, led by Tedros, responded quickly.
The Secretary of State, speaking remotely, announced sanctions.
distractor_probes: The Prime Minister addressed Parliament yesterday.
UNICEF issued a warning about malnutrition.
Maria Lopez, however, opened the session late.

results.hypothesis: The feature is activated by commas after multi-word noun phrases ending in proper nouns or title words, particularly in news-style descriptions of locations and offices.
positive_probes: The governor's office, Sacramento, issued a statement.
City Hall, New York, remained under tight security.
The prime minister's residence, Downing Street, welcomed diplomats.
The regional headquarters, Los Angeles, announced new layoffs.
The mayor's press office, San Francisco, denied the rumors.
distractor_probes: The governor's office in Sacramento issued a statement.
City Hall remained under tight security in New York.
The mayor's press office denied the rumors yesterday.

results.hypothesis: The feature fires on a comma immediately after a place/jurisdiction name used as a standalone NP in formal/news text, especially county/city names or institutional-location phrases like 'Schenectady,' and 'Albany,'.
positive_probes: Albany, approved the emergency budget late Tuesday.
Schenectady, reported three new cases overnight.
Orange County, issued a boil-water advisory Monday.
Rochester, announced a downtown redevelopment initiative.
Albany Medical Center, released the trial results yesterday.
distractor_probes: Officials in Albany approved the emergency budget Tuesday.
The Albany office released the trial results yesterday.
Schenectady reported three new cases overnight.

results.hypothesis: The feature may detect institutional or legal/government prose mentioning jurisdictions or offices, with extra boost when a comma follows the jurisdiction phrase.
positive_probes: Under California law, the agency shall issue notices.
In the State of Texas, the Secretary may approve filings.
Pursuant to federal regulations, the Office shall maintain records.
Within Cook County, the Department is authorized to inspect premises.
In the Commonwealth of Virginia, the Commission may impose penalties.
distractor_probes: California sunshine brightened the office courtyard after lunch.
The county fair office sold tickets near the entrance.
Federal style furniture filled the secretary's downtown apartment.

results.hypothesis: The feature is not a general appositive-comma or title/person separator; if anything, it is narrowly tied to location/jurisdiction names near office titles rather than generic apposition.

distractor_probes: My brother, Greg Abbott, addressed reporters yesterday.
The governor, Greg Abbott, addressed reporters yesterday.
